title: Pool Water Level Filling Simulation
description: The user stands beside an empty swimming pool and must fill it to precise water levels using water bottles. Players click to grab water bottles from a rack, carry them to the pool edge, pour them in by tilting, and must reach three target water level markers without overfilling. A temperature gauge and evaporation mechanic add complexity.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load 'shared_assets/pool.glb' centered in the scene and 'shared_assets/WaterBottle.glb' scaled appropriately so the bottle is roughly 1/8 the pool size. Set up a perspective camera at a 45-degree elevated angle looking down at the pool. Add ambient light intensity 0.6, a directional light casting shadows, and a warm point light near a temperature dial UI element. Create a translucent blue plane inside the pool representing the water surface that rises as bottles are poured. Place a rack of 8 clickable water bottle instances along one side of the pool. Implement these interaction steps: (1) Click a bottle on the rack to pick it up, attaching it to the cursor with raycasting. (2) Drag the bottle over the pool edge, validated by checking the bottle position is within pool bounds. (3) Press R to tilt and pour, triggering a particle stream animation from the bottle mouth downward. (4) The water plane rises proportionally, each bottle adding exactly 12.5% capacity. (5) A UI slider controls simulated temperature from 20-40C; higher temps cause an evaporation rate that slowly lowers the water level over time using a requestAnimationFrame loop. (6) The user must hit three target markers at 25%, 50%, and 87.5% shown as colored lines on the pool interior walls. (7) Pressing spacebar locks in the current level for validation against the target with a +/-3% tolerance. (8) If overfilled past the current target, a drain button appears to release 6.25% water per click. Display an HTML overlay HUD showing current water percentage, current target, temperature, evaporation rate, and bottles remaining. Add a subtle wave animation to the water surface using vertex displacement with sine functions. Each successful target lock triggers a green flash confirmation. All three targets must be hit in order to complete the simulation with a congratulations modal.
